source.title: Shape Matters: Understanding the Implicit Bias of the Noise Covariance
source.authors: Jeff Z. HaoChen; Colin Wei; J. Lee; Tengyu Ma

record.tranche_reason: The study compares added label noise and spherical Gaussian noise as ways to change generalization under large-batch training, using different methods and measures from the large-batch claim.
record.gate_note: The CIFAR100 VGG19 and quadratic-model noise comparisons report outcomes relevant to V5. Prior-work claims in the introduction and related-work section are not rows. Figure 1 reports several Gaussian-noise settings but does not map individual outcomes to each variance.
record.test_reason: The VGG19 experiment bears on V5's recipe dependence: added label noise recovers small-batch accuracy, whereas spherical Gaussian noise leaves most of the gap. All runs receive equal update counts, so the experiment does not directly test V5's fixed-epoch assertion.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. More precisely, the authors prove that parameter-dependent label noise can recover sparse ground truth in their quadratic model under specified conditions, whereas spherical Gaussian noise lacks sufficient implicit bias. They use this theory to explain their empirical noise-shape comparisons in deep networks.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares added label noise and spherical Gaussian noise with minibatch and full-batch baselines; it does not reproduce the original large-batch studies' recipe comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: Noise shape changes the outcome: label noise or minibatch noise performs better than spherical Gaussian noise. The CIFAR100 experiment uses VGG19, batch size 26 or 256, and disables weight decay and BatchNorm while retaining standard data augmentation.

fits_no_version.finding: In synthetic quadratically parameterized sparse regression, label noise and simulated minibatch noise improve recovery over noiseless full-gradient training and tuned spherical Gaussian noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Parameter-dependent noise can induce a stronger generalization-promoting implicit bias than spherical Gaussian noise in overparameterized sparse regression.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorems 2.1 and 2.2 establish sparse recovery with suitable label noise and learning-rate schedules, and nonexistence of a proper Gibbs distribution for the stated Gaussian-noise setting.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Noise covariance can determine implicit bias and recovery in quadratically parameterized models; these results do not establish magnitude-aware sharpness rankings.

record.problems: The deep-network comparison is limited to VGG19 on CIFAR100. Figure 1's individual Gaussian-noise variance outcomes are not stated in text, and no uncertainty estimates are reported. The results do not test fixed-epoch comparisons across a range of batch sizes.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible results on the versions were reported in the supplied text. Prior-work findings cited in the introduction and related-work section were excluded.

untested.parts: Coexistence of fixed random-label memorization and natural-label generalization; chance-level held-out performance with random labels.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under different tuning regimes.
Matched-epoch batch-size comparisons, workload-dependent batch thresholds, language models, longer-training interventions, learning-rate scaling with warmup, and normalization interventions.
Dropout interventions and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its correlation with generalization gaps, and rankings against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removal of examples selected by label-memorization influence versus random removal.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for any listed version. The approximately 13-point appendix gap and approximately 15-point caption improvement are approximate descriptions, not separate precise estimates. Gaussian noise's weak mitigation does not itself limit V5, which does not promise that every noise intervention succeeds. The unmatched epoch budgets prevent a verdict on V5's fixed-epoch batch penalty.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Language models, fixed epoch-budget comparisons across batch sizes, and longer training or other recipe adaptations.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures.

relationships.condition: VGG19 on CIFAR100, batch 256 with combined label-flipping and output-gradient noise, equal update counts
relationships.reason: R1–R3 show that this recipe recovers small-batch accuracy, supporting V5's adaptation component; fixed-epoch recovery is untested.
relationships.display_finding: The combined noise recipe recovered small-batch accuracy when all batch sizes used the same number of updates. Larger batches therefore made more passes through the training data.
